hints: Use $\tan^2x=\sec^2x-1$ before integrating the right side.
Apply $y=0$ at $x=0$ to determine the constant in the integrated relation.
Set $x=\pi/4$, then isolate $e^{2y}$ and take logarithms to calculate $y$.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables in $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \mathrm{e}^{-2y}\tan^2 x$ by dividing by $\mathrm{e}^{-2y}$ and multiplying by $\mathrm{d}x$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{2y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \tan^2 x\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Use the trigonometric identity $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$ to compute the right-hand integral:
$$\int \tan^2 x\,\mathrm{d}x = \int (\sec^2 x - 1)\,\mathrm{d}x = \tan x - x$$

Combine into the general solution:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{2y} = \tan x - x + c$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 0$ and $y = 0$ to determine $c$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^0 = \tan 0 - 0 + c \implies \dfrac{1}{2}(1) = 0 + c \implies c = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Write the particular solution:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{2y} = \tan x - x + \dfrac{1}{2} \implies \mathrm{e}^{2y} = 2\tan x - 2x + 1$$

Take natural logarithms and solve for $y$:
$$2y = \ln(1.429204) \approx 0.357117$$
$$y = \dfrac{0.357117}{2} \approx 0.178558$$

Round the value of $y$ to 3 decimal places:
$$y = 0.179$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Separates variables and integrates of either integral. Derives term $\frac12e^{2y}$. The final result is $\frac12e^{2y}=\tan x-x+\frac12$. When $x=\frac14\pi$, $y=0.179$. The final result is $\frac12e^{2y}=\tan x-x+\frac12$; when $x=\frac14\pi$, $y=0.179$.
